blocks.text: Verses 19–31 portray disaster through intensely embodied and world-shaping images: inner anguish, alarms of war, ruined tents and cities, a land returned to waste and darkness, and Daughter Zion gasping in labor-like pain. The passage also shifts among divine speech, a first-person anguished voice, communal language, and the personified city. These changing voices and images present catastrophe as something experienced across personal, communal, and even cosmic dimensions rather than as a detached report.
